To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) IL2 and IL4 induce the outgrowth of distinct T-cell subpopulations, 2) these subpopulations are functionally distinct with regard to their cytokine secretion pattern, and 3) the cytokine-specific mRNA expression of both subpopulations is differentially regulated by IL4.
the cytokine expression profile of PBL propagated in vitro with IL2 or IL-4 is different and can be modulated by shifting PBL from IL2 to IL4.

1) PBL cultured with rhIL2 or rhIL-4 for 8 days in the presence of anti-IL4 and anti-IFN gamma antibodies, respectively, are phenotypically and functionally distinct, and 2) these cells can be propagated in vitro for at least 14 days with the original cytokine, and 3) cells cultured with rhIL4 for 14 days in the presence or absence of rhIL2 show a similar mRNA expression pattern.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the induction and regulation of cytokine gene expression in T cells.
the development of an in vitro model system for studying the differentiation and function of distinct T cell phenotypes.
the identification of the cellular source of the different cytokines in human PBL.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the present study does not allow the identification of a human equivalent of murine Th1 and Th2 cells.

the cytokine mRNA expression profile in PBL after IL2 or IL 4 treatment is different, and that this difference is not a direct effect of the cytokine on the cells, but rather the result of a selective outgrowth.
IL2 and IL4 are not interchangeable in their capacity to promote the growth of T cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cytokine profile induced after PMA/I0-stimulation of T-IL4-cultures was similar to that of T helper cells (Th0) and T-IL2-cultures to Th1 cells.
the T-IL2 phenotype is characterised by a strong induction of IFN-gamma and GM-CSF, whereas the T-IL4 phenotype is characterised predominantly by the expression of IL-3 and IL-4.
T cells are not committed to express a specific set of cytokines, but that the pattern of cytokine expression can be modulated in response to environmental signals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
IL4 can induce IL3 expression in human T cells.
IL2 and IL4 are not equivalent in terms of their capacity to induce cytokine expression in human T cells.
IL2 and IL4 are capable of inducing distinct cytokine mRNA profiles in human peripheral blood mononuclear cells.
